_comment: The register of packages that OWE an invariant declaration. Read by package_invariants_check.py. It lives here, outside every package it records, for one reason: deleting a package's own INVARIANTS.yaml must not also delete the record that the package owes one. A missing declaration is a refusal (UNDECLARED), never 'this package has no constraints'. The comparison against what is on disk is EXACT-SET EQUALITY in both directions, so this file can neither quietly absorb a new package (UNLEDGERED) nor quietly forget an old one. Adding a package is free and takes two edits; removing one takes three, the third being the named membership constant in programs/tests/test_package_invariants_check.py.

packages.why: the landing gates and their plumbing; the rules bind what this code does, and both were measured here
a command whose frontmatter is malformed is loaded, is readable, and is never offered to a user
these scripts run on every session start; a non-zero exit refuses the session
the drivers' JSON-IO contract, stated in their own docstrings and enforced nowhere until now
a verbatim vendored copy; nothing outside the directory knows that, which is why the rule is inside it
the flat-namespace form, so a rule can bind a subsystem of the 1200-file programs/ tree without moving a file
